title: AI Detection Software Guidance by UT Austin
author: AI Learn Insights
summary: The University of Texas at Austin has issued a concise one-page policy on AI detection software that takes a clear institutional position: the primary focus should be on fostering academic integrity through effective course and assessment design, not through increasingly complex policing of students. The guidance prohibits instructors from using any third-party AI detection software to evaluate student work unless a university contract or purchase order is in place, and specifies that UT Austin has no such central contracts. A significant privacy and intellectual property dimension is highlighted: UT Austin students own the copyright and intellectual property of work they create in courses, meaning that submitting student work -- even anonymized -- to detection software without a university contract may violate those rights. Personal liability is also addressed: instructors who purchase AI detection software on personal or university procurement cards may be personally liable for any damages or legal costs if the purchase violates the university's policies. The overall stance positions institutional AI policy as primarily a question of pedagogy and course design rather than surveillance and enforcement.
points: * UT Austin's primary policy principle is that academic integrity should be fostered through effective course and assessment design, not through policing -- a model statement for institutional AI policy. * UT Austin prohibits instructors from using any AI detection software without a university contract; the university has no central contracts with any active AI detection software. * Students own the copyright and intellectual property of their coursework; submitting it to third-party detection software without a proper university contract may violate those rights. * Instructors who purchase AI detection software personally may be personally liable for damages or legal costs resulting from that purchase. * The policy implicitly frames AI detection as a losing game pedagogically and legally, redirecting faculty energy toward designing assessments that are resistant to AI completion in the first place.
quotes: The general philosophy Academic Affairs promotes is that the primary focus should be on fostering academic integrity through effective course and assessment design rather than by engaging in increasingly complex efforts to police students.

Submitting student work (even if it is anonymized) into any AI Detection Software without a University contract or purchase order in place may be a violation of that student's copyright and intellectual property rights.
The University prohibits the use of all third-party software, including AI Detection Software, to evaluate student work or assignments unless a University contract or purchase order is in place.
Instructors who purchase AI Detection Software on a personal credit card or a Procard may be personally liable for paying any damages or legal costs which may occur because of the purchase.
